note: Groups Heirloom means to cover. status: done (every mark has an entry), partial (pages exist, entries incomplete), not started. Keep 'why' to one line.

groups.name: British date letters: London, Birmingham, Sheffield, Chester
groups.why: Letters to 1923 have Chaffers facsimiles; 1924-2000 mostly typeface renderings, four cycles photographed; 2001-2026 added (no images)

groups.name: Edinburgh, Glasgow and Dublin date letters
groups.why: Edinburgh 1681-2026, Glasgow 1681-1963, Dublin 1638-1991 added 2026-11-25 (two of four readings agree on each row); Jackson facsimiles to about 1920; Dublin after 1991 not yet

groups.name: Exeter, Newcastle, York, Norwich date letters (closed offices)
groups.why: Exeter, Newcastle, York, Norwich and London before 1678 added 2026-11-25 with Jackson facsimiles; years only one reading gives are left out

groups.name: British makers' marks directory
groups.why: Jackson 1921's 7,833 marks plus 421 later makers from Pickford's pocket Jackson (1991); 1,084 Jackson records confirmed by Pickford, the rest single-source; makers after the 1920s only where Pickford lists them

groups.name: British import marks and sponsors' marks on foreign watch cases (e.g. R.W.C. Ltd for Rolex)
groups.why: New entry type; lead: Deutsches Uhrenmuseum Furtwangen inv. 2004-080 (CC BY-SA 4.0), a 1927 Rolex Oyster case back with British import marks and R.W.C. Ltd

groups.name: American makers' marks: manufacturers' trademarks (Jewelers' Circular 1896) and early silversmiths (Okie 1928)
groups.why: 2026-11-25: 403 trademarks of sterling, plate, watch-case and jewelry firms from the 1896 trade-mark book; early silversmiths from Okie with French 1917 as second source; later JC editions (1904-1922) are on HathiTrust only; 2026-11-26: 134 early silversmiths' marks photographed from The Met's CC0 collection (marks/met/), and the Jewelers' Circular groups cut apart one mark each

groups.name: American silver-plate makers
groups.why: Five pages written; marks need one crop each

groups.name: Old Sheffield (fused) plate makers, 1740s-1860s
groups.why: 2026-11-25: 235 marks of 200-odd platers from Okie (1928); Bradbury's list (pp. 98-112) not yet matched as a second source

groups.name: Silver standards: 925, 800, coin, Britannia, German silver
groups.why: Five pages written; marks need one crop each

groups.name: Mexican, French, German, Russian, Gorham, Christofle
groups.why: Seven pages written; several marks described in words only

groups.name: Tiffany, Reed & Barton, Towle, Wallace, Whiting, Kirk date marks
groups.why: us-year-marks.json (2026-11-25): Reed & Barton 1928-57 and Stieff 1901-88 from Rainwater and Kovels, Whiting 1905-24 (Rainwater only), Tiffany's president letters; Rainwater and Kovels show no year marks for Towle, Wallace, Kirk, Durgin or Dominick & Haff

groups.name: Continental silver marks: France, Germany, Austria, Hungary, Belgium, Holland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Russia, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Portugal
groups.why: continental-silver.json (2026-11-25): 2,189 town, standard, duty marks and date letters from Okie (1928), most with a facsimile; single-source until checked against Rosenberg (1922, downloaded) or national lists; 20th-century national marks (Dutch, Austro-Hungarian, Italian) not yet

groups.name: Chinese export, Indian and Japanese silver marks
groups.why: Indian silver, BIS hallmarks and origin stamps done 2026-11-25 (indian.json, its own table); Chinese export and Japanese silver not started

groups.name: Weller, Roseville, McCoy, Hull, Meissen, Hummel, Limoges, Haviland, Royal Doulton, Royal Copenhagen, Nippon, Noritake

groups.name: Pewabic Pottery, Detroit (marks/pewabic.json, group ceramics-makers)
groups.why: 29 marks, labels and signatures, 16 pictured (9 photographs incl. crops from DIA base photos, 4 book facsimiles, 3 Heirloom drawings after museum photos); 13 still need a base photo (Freer, UMMA, Henry Ford, Cranbrook need permission), and modern Pewabic's stamps since 1983 are undocumented (a question for Pewabic's archivist)

groups.name: Staffordshire potters and backstamps (Meakin, Johnson Brothers, Wood & Sons, Spode, Royal Crown Derby)
groups.why: 2026-11-25: 612 marks of 33 firm families (Johnson Bros., Meakin, Mason's, Wedgwood, Spode, Copeland, Ridgway, Minton, Royal Albert, Shelley and others) from Godden (1964), 425 drawn from the book; single-source until Cushion & Honey (1956) or Kovel (1986) is matched mark by mark; the long tail of smaller potters, and marks after 1964, not yet
